minutes.headline: Assessors voted to adopt the three-year average worksheet for abatements, three to nothing, a day before the filing deadline.
minutes.summary: Held the day before the abatement filing deadline, the meeting was mostly about residents' anger over large waterfront assessment increases. Residents asked about inspections, hearings, deadline extensions and whether the board has confidence in the assessments. The board voted to approve the Appellate Tax Board three-year average worksheet, then signed motor vehicle excise abatements.

public_comment.topic: Corrected social media claims: the meeting was properly posted, scheduled in line with past practice, and is only about adopting the worksheet. He asked the board to allow placeholders on abatement applications.
Asked who will do the inspections and whether they will be certified. He asked that abatement filers get a hearing before the board.
Asked how many abatement forms were filed and whether all fit in the 90 days.
Asked whether assessors would visit homes to confirm public record data is correct.
Asked how to get data withheld pending the investigation. He asked that hearings be formalized later and confirmed the assessed value reflects January 1, 2022.
Asked whether an abatement inspection means reassessment next year, given the revaluation schedule.
Asked how abatement forms will be ordered for review.

public_comment.stated_role: vice chair, board of Selectmen, 284 Lancaster Avenue
public_comment.topic: Asked for the board of assessors' official position on the assessments and on a reassessment.
Said it may be premature for the board to state confidence or no confidence before abatement applications are reviewed.
Called the blanket increase on lake properties a red flag. He questioned whether land was viewed before assessment and asked about site index codes.
Asked the town to reverse in-house assessing and go back to outsourcing it.
Asked who decides abatements and how inspections differ from appraisals.
Said lake land varies in frontage, depth and quality. He urged assessors to create categories to evaluate it.
Asked whether non-lakefront sales that also sold high would be looked at.
Questioned the sales used in the waterfront valuation, including a two-family home and sales not on the published list.
Pointed out the abatement form's wording on fair cash value as of January 1st, and urged the board to consider a no-confidence position. He cited independent appraisals well below the town's.
Argued the certification standards leave room for interpretation of the data.
Asked whether lakefront values affect the rest of the town. He asked that information on senior exemptions and deferrals be shared publicly.

votes.motion: Approve use of the Massachusetts Appellate Tax Board three-year average worksheet

budget_items.what_was_said: The count of filed abatement applications rose over a few days, and the board expects hundreds to handle within the statutory window.
A resident called a blanket increase on all lake properties a red flag.
A resident questioned the sales used to build the valuation, including one home that may be a two-family.
A former selectman said assessing was outsourced for many years until it was brought in-house, and asked that the decision be reversed.

decisions.decision: The principal assessor and a member said the board would make liberal use of its ability to extend the 90-day abatement deadlines.
Board members said they would accept additional information on an abatement until it is decided, if the application is filed by the deadline and notes that more is coming.
Request that the right to appear at hearings be formalized at a future meeting. No commitment was made at this meeting.
The board will not make an official statement of position on the assessments. A member gave a personal view that the system has flaws.
Real estate exemptions are confidential and will be taken up in executive session at a future meeting. Motor vehicle excise abatements were signed at this meeting.
The board meets monthly, and residents were told to bring questions back to later meetings.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted 3-0 to approve the Appellate Tax Board three-year average worksheet for abatements, the day before the filing deadline.
The principal assessor and a member said the board would make liberal use of its ability to extend the 90-day abatement deadlines.
Board members said they would accept added information on an abatement until it is decided, if the application is filed on time and notes more is coming.
The board declined to make an official statement of position on the waterfront assessments; a member gave a personal view that the system has flaws.
Motor vehicle excise abatements were signed; real estate exemptions are confidential and go to a future executive session.

why_it_matters: Owners who think a waterfront or lake assessment is too high can still file an abatement application by the deadline, and the board said it would accept supporting material afterward.
Residents asked for hearings, a position on the assessments and a look at the sales used in the valuation. The board made no commitment on any of these at this meeting.
watch_next: A future meeting where the board said it would take up formalizing the right to appear at abatement hearings.
A future executive session on real estate exemptions; the board meets monthly.
